close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: aligned ContactCardComparator with the 3-sibling consensus (TaskComparator, TaskNotificationComparator, CalendarEventComparator) — added PartialEq, Eq, Default derives and renamed default_true → default_ascending. Workspace canonical-template rule honored.
description:
ContactCardComparator (card.rs:325-337) is the cookie-cutter outlier among extension-types sibling comparators.

| Aspect | CalendarEventComparator | TaskComparator | TaskNotificationComparator | ContactCardComparator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| derive PartialEq, Eq | yes | yes | yes | NO |
| derive Default | yes | yes | yes | NO |
| default fn name | default_ascending | default_ascending | default_ascending | default_true |

Four siblings, three use the identical idiom. ContactCardComparator is the fourth and uses a different idiom. Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates': differences between extension-types siblings should be 'the specific JMAP capability the crate covers, nothing else'. Comparator derives and helper-fn names are not capability-specific.

Fix: add #[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Default)] to ContactCardComparator, rename default_true → default_ascending. ContactCardComparator::default() with property == '' is meaningless on the wire but matches the sibling pattern; if Default is genuinely undesired here, file that finding instead and remove it from CalendarEventComparator/TaskComparator/TaskNotificationComparator for symmetry — but the canonical template direction is the simpler change.

EmailComparator in jmap-mail-types is a separate shape (typed ComparatorProperty enum, ::new() constructor, Keyword field) because RFC 8621 has many more mandated properties — it is not the relevant canonical for this finding.
title: ContactCardComparator diverges from canonical sibling comparator shape
